sources.title: Jakub Zejmis, Belarus in the 1920s: Ambiguities of National Formation
sources.note: Peer-reviewed account of the restored BSSR, institutions, Belarusian cultural development, Sovietization and the 1925 exile-government accommodation.

sources.title: Oxford Academic, Soviet Belarus: the BSSR
sources.note: Current scholarly synthesis of Soviet Belarus formation, 1920s cultural revival, integration into the USSR and Stalinist purges.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Belarus and Moldova: Country Studies
sources.note: Federal Research Division synthesis checked for war, partition, the BSSR, Belarusization, Stalinist policies and western Belarus under Poland.

sources.title: League of Nations Treaty Series, Treaty of Peace signed at Riga, 18 March 1921
sources.note: Official published treaty text fixing the Polish-Soviet frontier and extending Russian and Ukrainian undertakings specifically to Belarus.

sources.title: United Nations, Belarus member state
sources.note: Official UN record confirms the Byelorussian SSR existed internationally after the atlas 1938 seam and became a founding UN member in 1945.

sources.title: Library of Congress Law Library, Treaty on the Creation of the Soviet Union
sources.note: Legal history of the 30 December 1922 union treaty signed by Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian federation.

sources.title: Russian State Archive, 1920 Declaration of Soviet Belarus
sources.note: Digitized primary archival record of the 1920 declaration restoring the Soviet Socialist Republic of Belarus.

sources.title: Per Anders Rudling, The Rise and Fall of Belarusian Nationalism, 1906 to 1931
sources.note: Scholarly monograph checked for repeated statehood declarations, Belarusization, national institutions and Stalinist suppression.

sources.title: University of Pittsburgh Press excerpt, The Rise and Fall of Belarusian Nationalism
sources.note: Publisher excerpt explains partition, Belarusian national formation and the onset of Stalinist transformation by 1931.

sources.title: 1927 Constitution of the Belarusian SSR facsimile
sources.note: Public-domain scan used for the exact Belarusian title sample, document date, original spelling and material appearance.

sources.title: National Legal Internet Portal of Belarus, Constitution of 1927
sources.note: Official legal-history page paired with the primary scan for constitutional date, polity context and original Belarusian title.

sources.title: Archontology, Belarus polity style 1920 to 1991
sources.note: Reference chronology checked for original Belarusian polity spelling, transliteration, four-language provision and word-order changes.

sources.title: Library Assembly of Eurasia, National Library of Belarus
sources.note: Institutional history records the library founding within Belarusian State University in 1922, initial holdings and early readers.

sources.title: Math-Net.Ru, Belarusian State University
sources.note: Academic directory history records the university founding in 1921 and the creation of several specialist institutes in the 1920s and 1930s.

sources.title: Oleh Kazak, Minsk Polish Pedagogical Technical School, 1922 to 1937
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of teacher training for Polish-language schools within Soviet Belarus and its national-cultural policy context.

sources.title: Elissa Bemporad, Becoming Soviet Jews: The Bolshevik Experiment in Minsk
sources.note: Scholarly monograph on Yiddish schooling, work, gender, religion, family continuity, Sovietization and terror in interwar Minsk.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia, Belarus
sources.note: Scholarly reference for the republic four official languages and Jewish cultural and institutional life.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia, Minsk
sources.note: City evidence for Yiddish schools, kindergarten, theater, publishing, scholarship and a four-language railway-station sign.

sources.title: YIVO Encyclopedia, Soviet Yiddish-Language Schools
sources.note: Scholarly chronology of mother-tongue schooling in Belorussia, rising enrollment, secular curriculum and the 1938 liquidation.

sources.title: Aliaksandr Huzhalouski, Destroying Family: Sexual Revolution in 1920s Soviet Belarus
sources.note: Belarusian Historical Review article on family debate, marriage, sexuality, periodical evidence and homeless children in the 1920s.

sources.title: University of Warsaw repository, Belarusian Worker and Peasant Woman
sources.note: Academic study of a 1924 to 1939 BSSR magazine and its changing public ideal for women family, economic, social and political roles.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Minsk
sources.note: Museum account and Dora Rivkina profile provide a bounded 1933 to 1939 glimpse of one Minsk family, school, dance, swimming and Young Pioneers.

sources.title: Russian Ethnographic Museum, Belarusians in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century
sources.note: Museum object-based description of rural houses, stoves, food preparation, homespun clothing and gendered crafts, used with an early-period continuity warning.

sources.title: Communes, hostels and barracks: communal living in Soviet cities
sources.note: Academic chapter on proposed and experienced forms of Soviet urban communal housing in the 1920s.

sources.title: Built Heritage, Minsk wooden suburbs as urban heritage
sources.note: Archive-based urban study of worker suburbs, 1923 housing redistribution, migration and wooden housing, with later plumbing evidence used only as a cautious continuity clue.

sources.title: Dzmitry Kryvashei, Daily Routine of a Belarusian Official in the 1920s and 1930s
sources.note: Period-specific research on office hours, Belarusization, wages, ration cards, workplace assistance and organized leisure in the BSSR.

sources.title: Hoover Institution, The Adventures of the ARA in Minsk
sources.note: Archival narrative of American Relief Administration work in Belarus from 1920 to 1923 and dependence of hospitals and children homes on relief.

sources.title: Ann E. Healy, Belarus in Crisis: Medicine and Relief after War
sources.note: Archive-based study of clinics, orphanages, vaccines, disinfecting machines, baths, soap, water purification and medical shortages in early Soviet Belarus.

sources.title: Andrei Zamoiski, Face to the Countryside: Healthcare in Soviet Belarus
sources.note: Archive-based study of rural doctors, feldshers, maternity care, sports, unsafe water, sanitation campaigns, folk healers and coercion from the 1920s through 1930s.

sources.title: Formation and development of the State pharmacy service in Minsk, 1918 to 1944
sources.note: Peer-reviewed pharmacy history with documented 1920 nationalization and staff counts for the Minsk pharmacy administration in 1925 and 1926.

sources.title: Lynne Viola, Peasant Rebels Under Stalin
sources.note: Archive-based scholarly account of forced collectivization and varied peasant resistance across the Soviet Union from 1928 to 1932.

sources.title: Andrei Zamoiski, The Polish Peasantry in Soviet Belarus
sources.note: Peer-reviewed BSSR case study of Polish rural communities during the transition from NEP to forced collectivization.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Internal Workings of the Soviet Union
sources.note: Archival exhibit covering industrialization, collectivization, famine, religious persecution, censorship and the Great Terror.

sources.title: Sciences Po, Kurapaty: NKVD Mass Killings in Soviet Belarus
sources.note: Research encyclopedia entry on Belarusian partition, Stalinist repression and the evidence and estimate disputes surrounding Kurapaty.

sources.title: The Historical Journal, Understanding Stalin Terror against Western Minorities
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review of the 1937 to 1938 NKVD national operations and their impact on Poles, Belarusians, Ukrainians and other targeted people.

sources.title: Universal Lithuanian Encyclopedia, Cinema of Belarus
sources.note: Encyclopedia chronology for Belgoskino, early newsreels, the first feature film and production outside Minsk because local facilities were limited.

sources.title: The Family, the Body, and the Self: Jewish life in the Soviet 1920s
sources.note: Open scholarly book with travel accounts of Minsk-region family life, food and clothing plus evidence of unequal access for disenfranchised households.

sources.title: Hoover Institution, A True Picture of Famine and Revival
sources.note: Curated archive explains the scope and limits of ARA photographs documenting famine relief and daily life in 1922 and 1923.

proposedOverrides.summary: Soviet Belarus or the Byelorussian SSR in the atlas 1920 to 1938 display window, with a documented 1930 geometry error.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact id is preserved, but White Russia is identified as an old English exonym for Belarus or Belorussia, not the anti-Bolshevik White movement.
The 1920 Polygon is Belarus-sized and includes Minsk, Vitebsk, Mogilev, Gomel, Polotsk and Slutsk while excluding Brest and Grodno under the separate Poland feature.
The 1930 MultiPolygon is a severe source-data mismatch covering most of the USSR, including Moscow, Leningrad, Kyiv, Crimea, Omsk and Irkutsk. It is not treated as Belarusian territory.
The 1938 replacement by ussr is a display seam. The override records fell null, continuity status and no inferred predecessor or successor links.
The researched subject is the Soviet Socialist Republic of Belarus and Byelorussian SSR during 1920 to 1938, not all Belarusian people, western Belarus under Poland or later independent Belarus.
The writing sample is the exact Belarusian title of the 1927 constitution in period Cyrillic spelling, with transliteration, translation and a multilingual-population caveat.
Daily life distinguishes town and countryside, family and institution, different language and faith communities, relief-era evidence and the changing 1920s to 1930s political climate.
